title: Brown Rice with Soy‑Based Sauce, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product obtained from unrefined rice kernels. In this version it is served with a soy‑based sauce prepared without added fat, preserving the natural flavor and nutritional profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ layers, giving it more fiber and micronutrients than white rice.
Soy sauce is traditionally fermented from soybeans, wheat, salt and water, a process that can last from months to years.
The lack of added fat makes the dish low‑calorie while still providing protein and complex carbs.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.
Soy sauce naturally contains amino acids such as glutamate, which enhance the umami taste.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Brown rice provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and cholesterol management.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs deliver sustained energy, beneficial for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Contains magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals aid muscle function, nerve signaling, and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Together, brown rice and soy sauce provide a complete set of amino acids useful for vegetarians.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products, including soy sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Traditional soy sauce can be high in salt; choose a low‑sodium version if needed.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, drizzled with the soy sauce. It can be added to salads, bowls, soups, or used as a side for vegetables and lean protein. Garnish with sliced green onions or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with sauce should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3‑4 days.
